key_insight: Minimum dissipation in driven stationary states and maximum dissipation during frozen-state relaxation arise from the same convex, minimized Rayleighian framework.
engineering_relevance: The framework clarifies how variational formulations can recover viscous-flow equations, including inertia under suitable constraints.
method: Analyze thermodynamic extremal principles across stationary and relaxation regimes.
Use the Reynolds transport theorem to formulate continuum energy rates.
Hold inertial driving forces fixed during variation and use material coordinates for Navier–Stokes flow.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical tests on Stokes, unsteady Stokes, Navier–Stokes flow, and dissipative Lagrangian mechanics, rather than numerical benchmarks or experimental data.
watch_item: With inertia, an extremal statement requires the frozen driving force to be independent of the varied rate; the Eulerian convective term complicates direct application.
paper_title: Variational principles for dissipative continua: transport theorems, inertia, and the minimum-maximum duality
